newsitem.title: USA: US spot distillate diffs hold gains in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot distillate diffs hold gains in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast spot distillate differentials held most of the gains seen early in the day, while the rest of the Gulf and New York Harbor (NYH) markets were quiet.
Market players pointed to a modest short squeeze in USG heating oil and low sulphur diesel as the main reason for the firmer diffs.

USG heating oil for 9th cycle delivery on the Colonial Pipeline was talked on either side of 1.85 cents under the screen, up about 0.25 cent on the day, although traders said most of the action there took place early in the day.
USG low sulphur diesel also firmed as offers for 9th cycle barrels pulled back to 0.50 cents over the screen, a 0.25 cent increase from Thursday.
NYH low sulphur diesel diffs may have seen some strength in sympathy with the gains in Houston, as offers for prompt barrels moved to 4.00 cents over the screen, a gain of 0.25 cent.
Market players kept a close eye on developements in California, where 250,000 barrels a day in refinery production could be idled next week if workers at Unocal refineries begin a strike.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
